subject: SOC 2 Type II + cloud provider evidence — carve-out / bridge letter options
messages:
From: Emma Bradley <emma.bradley@datasync.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@datasync.io
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Request: SOC 2 Type II and cloud provider evidence

Hi Marissa,

We're preparing for our internal security review and need the following from Redwood to complete our vendor assessment:

- SOC 2 Type II report (most recent period) or an equivalent attestation
- Clarification on which cloud provider SOC reports Redwood relies on (AWS/GCP/Azure) and whether those are provided as carve-out or inclusive in your scope
- A bridge letter/attestation if the audit period doesn't cover our procurement window
- Subprocessor list and any shared-responsibility notes (specifically Snowflake, Datadog, and our AWS tenancy concerns)

Also looping in procurement for contract timing. Can you share a timeline for delivery? If you have a standard bridge letter template, that would speed things up.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Bradley
Senior IT Risk Manager
Datasync, Inc.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: SOC 2 Type II and cloud provider evidence

Folks — forwarding the Datasync ask. Quick bullets on what they want above. Proposed plan:

1) Provide Redwood SOC 2 Type II 2026 (redacted where necessary) — indicate audit window and controls that rely on cloud provider coverage.
2) Provide a short mapping doc that shows which controls are satisfied by Redwood vs. the cloud provider (AWS).
3) Offer a bridge letter if the audit window doesn't align; use our standard template and route via DocuSign.
4) Produce an export of subprocessors and a short narrative on shared responsibility for network isolation and tenant boundaries.

Questions for Rishi: can we rely on AWS SOC 2 in carve-out fashion for our public cloud infra, or do we treat some services as inclusive? Any blockers for giving a partial AWS report summary?

Lauren/Aditya — can you take the mapping and subprocessor export? I can assemble the bridge letter draft. Need this back to send to Datasync by EOD Friday 6/3.

Thanks,
Marissa
VP, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 12:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: SOC 2 Type II and cloud provider evidence

Marissa — short answers:

- We rely on AWS SOC 2 for infrastructure controls. For our customers the typical posture is a carve-out (i.e., AWS SOC covers the AWS-managed components).
- We also have coverage for certain managed services (RDS, EKS managed control plane) in our own report; Snowflake is a separate subprocessor and has its own attestations.
- No internal policy blocker to share a summary of the AWS report coverage; however, we do not share AWS's raw vendor report. We provide a Redwood-authored mapping ("AWS coverage summary") plus the list of referenced AWS controls.

I'll attach a one-page draft bridge-letter text (we use this to call out audit window differences) — counsel has approved the template previously but if Datasync requests auditor-signed bridge letters we can introduce ThirdLine (our auditor) for attestation.

I recommend we: provide (a) our SOC 2 Type II 2026 PDF (redacted), (b) mapping spreadsheet that lists controls / subservice delineation, (c) subprocessor export, and (d) bridge-letter template with DocuSign.

Rishi
Head of Trust & Controls
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Emma Bradley <emma.bradley@datasync.io>
Cc: procurement@datasync.io, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@thirdlineaudit.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 Type II and cloud provider evidence

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list. Per internal review and Rishi's notes, here's what we can deliver and the expected timeline: 

Deliverables (ETA to you):
- Redwood SOC 2 Type II report (period: 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31) — attached (Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf). We have redacted vendor-sensitive appendix pages; let us know if you need a controlled NDA for fuller access.
- AWS coverage summary (Redwood_AWS_SOC2_Relation_Summary.xlsx) — attached. This maps Redwood controls to AWS responsibilities and flags carve-out areas.
- Subprocessor list export (inline in sheet) — includes Snowflake, Datadog, Sentry, Stripe; fields show dataprocessing purpose and region.
- Bridge letter template (Draft_Bridge_Letter_Template.docx) — attached and pushed to DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/templates/abcd-bridge-letter. If you need an auditor-signed bridge letter we can coordinate with our auditor, Tom Bennett (copied).

Notes on carve-out: we treat AWS infrastructure as a carve-out for infrastructure maintenance controls; where Redwood manages configuration (IAM, KMS usage, application-level encryption), those controls are in-scope for Redwood and documented in the mapping. For Snowflake and other SaaS subprocessors we reference their attestations as part of the subprocessor evidence package.

If your review requires access to our auditor for clarifying scope/responsibility splits, Tom is available next week for a short call (cc'ed).

Timing: we aim to have the final DocuSign bridge letter and the completed mapping to you by Friday, 2027-06-03 EOD. Please advise if you have a hard procurement cutover prior to that date.

Best,
Marissa
VP, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf (pdf, 2.8MB stub), Redwood_AWS_SOC2_Relation_Summary.xlsx (xlsx), Draft_Bridge_Letter_Template.docx (docx)
From: Emma Bradley <emma.bradley@datasync.io>

Cc: procurement@datasync.io

Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 Type II and cloud provider evidence

Marissa — thank you, that is very helpful. A couple quick items:

- Can you confirm auditor contact info for a short scope call? (Tom Bennett copied)
- Our procurement cutoff is next Thursday 6/10; receiving the DocuSign bridge letter and the mapping by 6/3 works well.
- Can you also confirm whether logs (access/audit trail) for the last 90 days can be made available in a time-limited secure link if our auditors request them? If so, what is the expected turnaround?

If those are all yes, we'll proceed and share your materials internally.

Thanks again — appreciate the quick turnaround.
Emma
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Emma Bradley <emma.bradley@datasync.io>, Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@thirdlineaudit.com>

Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 Type II and cloud provider evidence

Emma — quick answers:

- Auditor contact: Tom Bennett, ThirdLine Audit — tom.bennett@thirdlineaudit.com. He is willing to do a 30-min scope call next week; I'll coordinate availability.
- Logs: yes — we can produce access/audit trail exports for the last 90 days on a time-limited secure transfer (SFTP with one-time creds or a signed link). Typical turnaround is 3 business days after formal request and execution of an NDA / access agreement. If Datasync wants us to push logs directly to your auditors, we can do so under a scoped data sharing agreement; we'll need a POA from procurement.

We'll finalize the DocuSign bridge letter and mapping tomorrow morning and send.

Thanks,
Marissa
